topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer welcomes the class, outlines the scope of the cancer lecture series, and introduces the key learning objectives regarding cancer causation and carcinogenicity.

topics.label: The Biological Nature of Cancer and Mutational Origins
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease influenced by the cellular microenvironment and introduce the primary mechanisms generating oncogenic mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and the Cancer Causation Debate
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how environmental exposures influence cancer incidence in the context of the scientific debate and epidemiological evidence comparing intrinsic replicative errors to preventable external factors.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Oncogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how biological pathogens contribute to malignancy through immune evasion, chronic inflammation, and genetic alteration, detailed through the paradigm of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical pathways by which chemical carcinogens and physical radiation cause DNA adducts and mutations, emphasizing the role of xenobiotic metabolism.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Carcinogenesis Mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain non-mutagenic drivers of cancer, focusing on how tumor promoters, chronic inflammation, and the developmental proliferative state of host tissues facilitate malignant outgrowth.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the complementary scientific strategies used to assess carcinogen exposure and prove carcinogenic potential across genomics, population epidemiology, animal bioassays, and in vitro tests.

topics.label: Conclusion: Risk-Benefit Analysis and Lecture Wrap-Up
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session by summarizing key concepts and framing carcinogen exposure as an everyday balance between risk and practical benefit.
